subject: Bridged commit resolution — capacity splitter proposal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, sales@cloudframe.io
Cc: eric.santos@auroracloud.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridged commit resolution — capacity splitter proposal

Team / CloudFrame —

Quick summary: CloudFrame and AuroraCloud have overlapping Dedicated commitments for Q3 in the same GPU pool (us-west-2, reserved cluster pool). Both deals ramp starting July 1; combined peak would exceed our committed capacity by ~60% during morning U.S. hours. We need an allocation plan so we can: 1) give a clear answer to procurement, 2) prevent noisy preemptions, and 3) avoid SLA churn.

I attached a working capacity model (capacity-model-v3.xlsx) and the SLA exception request from CloudFrame. High-level options I see:
- Proportional split by committed tokens (fair-share)
- Priority lane for CloudFrame (larger, existing commit) + preemptible buffer for Aurora
- Time-based windowing (e.g., CloudFrame peak 08:00–12:00, Aurora 12:00–20:00)

Questions for internal owners:
- Ben: what is the updated headroom in us-west-2 after recent infra reclaims? Can we free any unallocated reserved nodes between 08:00–12:00 PT?
- Karthik: for Dedicated deals, do we have contract language that forces a hard priority? If not, what's our default routing policy right now (priority by deal size / by signup timestamp / by premium band)?
- Grace: operations — what automation would be required to implement a time-windowed split (short term vs. longer-term)?

CloudFrame / Eric — I'd appreciate any flexibility on ramp windows. If you can shift part of the heaviest batch jobs to later in the day, that would substantially reduce conflict.

Goal: agree on a provisional splitter by EOD today so sales and procurement can align on credits/SLA notes.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: capacity-model-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA-exception-request.pdf (PDF)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, sales@cloudframe.io
Cc: eric.santos@auroracloud.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridged commit resolution — capacity splitter proposal

Naomi —

Quick note from infra: after yesterday's reclamation we freed roughly 18% headroom in the pool. That moves us from "over by 60%" to "over by ~42%" at projected peaks. No guarantees, but we can also delay a planned maintenance on 6/29 (adds ~6% if postponed one week).

Operational realities:
- We don't have a hard contractual priority mechanism unless legal added a priority clause per deal — most enterprise deals are silent and rely on verbal SLR negotiations.
- Default routing today is weighted by 'reserved commitment' then fall back to availability. That implies a de-facto favoring of larger commits but it's not enforced in code paths as an absolute preemption.

Short-term ask: If sales signs off on a time-windowed split, we can implement a routing rule in the control plane that enforces a 60/40 split (CloudFrame/Aurora) between 08:00–12:00. That is ~3 hours of engineering config + a quick runbook. Time-window enforcement would need an ops-side kill-switch.

I'll push a trimmed node release to postpone maintenance if Naomi approves.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Operations

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridged commit resolution — capacity splitter proposal

Naomi / Ben —

Thanks for the heads up. Short update from Aurora: our ramp is aggressive but not immovable. We have several large batch training jobs that are scheduled between 09:00–13:00 PT but can be shifted to start after 14:00 PT with about a week's notice to our SREs.

We are not comfortable with a permanent priority lane that would preempt our jobs without credits. If Redwood proposes a 60/40 short-term split during 08:00–12:00 for the first 6 weeks of ramp, Aurora would request a credit holdback and a rollback clause if latency exceeds thresholds for our clients. We prefer the time-window approach vs. arbitrary proportional preemption.

Also attaching (inbound) the minimal SLA exception file they sent — flagged the sections we care about.

—Eric
AuroraCloud — Head of Production

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: eric.santos@auroracloud.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridged commit resolution — capacity splitter proposal

Thanks, everyone — good progress. Summarizing decisions and next steps (provisional):

1) Short-term (first 6 weeks of July ramp): implement a time-windowed splitter that enforces 60% of pool capacity to CloudFrame and 40% to AuroraCloud during 08:00–12:00 PT. Outside that window, routing reverts to weighted reserved-commitment fallback.

2) Credits & rollback: Sales will draft a credit holdback and SLA rollback clause for AuroraCloud (Grace, can you please coordinate with Sales and Legal on the exact metric thresholds? I linked the HubSpot deal.)

3) Ops implementation: Ben, proceed with the routing rule change and postpone the 6/29 maintenance until 7/6. Ensure we have a kill-switch and an automated alert to the on-call if queue latencies exceed 300ms p50 for more than two consecutive 5-minute windows.

4) Follow-up: Naomi will host a 30-minute sync Monday 6/21 with SRE + Sales + Aurora to sign off on the window and credits. Please come with success criteria and rollback language.

If anyone strongly objects to the 60/40 provisional, flag now. Otherwise I'll update the HubSpot deal and send the credit note template to Eric after the sync.

—Naomi
